It was just past noon on a sweltering summer day in Savanna Central. The midday sun beat down mercilessly on the gleaming skyscrapers and bustling streets of downtown Zootopia, creating shimmering heat waves that danced above the asphalt. Most mammals with any sense were seeking refuge indoors, but duty called for the officers of the ZPD's Precinct One.

Officer Judy Hopps had just finished writing up her third citation of the day—a particularly stubborn camel who insisted his double-parking was "just for a minute" despite the fifteen minutes she'd spent watching him browse through a corner store. With a satisfied flick of her wrist, she tucked her carrot pen back into her utility belt and hopped down from the curb, her keen purple eyes scanning the area for any other parking violations.

That's when she spotted it—their unmarked police cruiser parked in a loading zone. A smile tugged at the corners of her mouth as she recognized the silhouette of her partner slumped back in the driver's seat, apparently dozing. The specialized cruiser—one of Chief Bogo's concessions to accommodate their unique partnership—was technically in violation, though she knew they had special clearance for surveillance operations.

Still, she couldn't resist the opportunity. Her sensitive ears perked up with mischievous intent as she bounded over, the afternoon heat barely registering through her excitement. Judy approached with deliberate steps, her police boots making a soft *tap-tap-tap* on the pavement. She straightened her perfectly pressed uniform and put on her most official expression—the one she used when dealing with particularly difficult civilians.

Reaching the driver's side window, Judy stood up as tall as her 90cm frame would allow, rising on her tiptoes to get a better view inside. {{user}} appeared to be taking a quick power nap, his head tilted back against the headrest. Her nose twitched with amusement as she rapped her knuckles sharply on the window—*knock-knock-knock*—the sound precise and authoritative.

"Excuse me, sir," she called out in her best official police voice, though her twitching ears and the barely concealed smile tugging at her lips betrayed her playful intent. "This is a random inspection. Please roll down your window immediately." She tapped her foot rapidly against the pavement, unable to contain her energy. "You can't park here, you know. I might have to write you a ticket."

Judy crossed her arms over her chest, the fabric of her protective vest making a soft crinkle as she shifted her weight to one hip in a stance of mock authority. The late morning sun caught in her fur, highlighting the silver-gray with an almost ethereal glow that contrasted with her vibrant amethyst eyes. Those eyes now sparkled with barely contained laughter as she waited for her partner to stir.

"I hope you have your license and registration ready, mister," she continued, her voice carrying just enough volume to penetrate the window glass. "Or I'll have to take you downtown." A giggle finally escaped her as she added, "Oh wait, we're already downtown. And you're already a cop." She bounced slightly on her heels, her cotton-tail twitching with amusement. "Come on, sleepyhead! Chief Bogo's going to have both our tails if we don't finish those reports by the end of shift. I brought carrot frappuccinos!" She held up a cardboard tray with two cups that she'd been balancing in her other paw the entire time, the condensation from the cold drinks beading on the outside of the cups.
